solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detectives do reprimand taking nothing down

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to do someone is to cheat or con them
to slate is to criticise harshly
zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Police officers giving a telling-off while refusing to write anything down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like the tail of 'taking nothing down' (not noting anything), but it is the definition, meaning sad. DIs are Detective Inspectors; to do someone is to con them.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means feeling low and dejected, a close synonym of being unhappy beyond comfort.

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to stoop to something is to deign to do it
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone bending over as they walk around little garden patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoops' and 'plots' both suggest gardening, but stoops is condescends and plots are schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots and designs are both schemes or secret plans, as in having designs on something.

clue.text: Relief derived from sap we gather

indicators.note: what we gather is what we have heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible fool, a sucker

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy extracted from plant sap, as the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' reads as plant juice, but it means a dupe, a sucker. SUCCOUR is said the same way in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help or aid given in hardship, a synonym for relief brought to someone in need.

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
nigh is an old word for nearly

explanation.surface: A question of whether revellers stay out in public almost till dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: an overnight stay lasts until morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overnight lasts through the dark hours from evening to the following dawn.

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone spoke, pronouncing words carefully with good diction from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the first letters spell the answer, and the clue describes words spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Said is the past tense of say, meaning uttered or voiced in speech, the same as spoke.

blocks.note: to stall is to delay or hang about
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A market stall that sells underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a market booth, but it is the verb to delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing and nightwear, a specific kind of underwear.

clue.text: Head, occasionally even in pith helmet

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the head of something is its top
the first and third letters of this word

explanation.surface: Now and then even a head sits inside a colonial sun helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb, but it is the source of the letters; take the odd ones, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee (or topi) is a lightweight sun hat made from pith, worn in hot colonial climates.

indicators.note: a little of something is only a part of it, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A tiny shrub growing on a Japanese miniature landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: saikei is a Japanese art of miniature planted landscapes, so a small tree on one is a bonsai.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a dwarfed tree or shrub grown in a container, the kind placed in a saikei scene.

indicators.note: being trapped inside means being held within, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: a vacant property is to let, available to rent
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody stuck inside a lavatory that showed as unoccupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacant' is the sign on a free cubicle, but here it means available to rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet and lavatory are direct synonyms for the room or fixture used for relieving oneself.

clue.text: Release from Queen rejected in part

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run backwards
being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a section is a part

explanation.surface: A statement put out by the palace, partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the standard crossword Queen; reversed to RE, it goes inside SECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretion is a substance a gland or cell discharges, so it is a release of fluid.

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the letters run the other way
to capture is to hold inside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: an op is a work, short for opus
hot means sexy, attractive

explanation.surface: Retouching a picture that has caught someone looking alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work over' sounds like editing a picture, but 'over' only turns the short word for a musical work round.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a snapshot, a quickly taken photograph.

indicators.note: the origin is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter
a sphere is round

explanation.surface: How our round planet came into being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' reads as the planet, which fits the globe imagery, but the answer means soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth and ground both mean the soil or land surface beneath one's feet.

clue.text: Cancellation of show containing empty rows

indicators.note: empty means with the insides removed, so only the outer letters remain
to contain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to show is to reveal
just the outside letters

explanation.surface: A theatre show is called off because many rows of seats are unsold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' sounds like a production but is the verb to reveal; RS sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of a decision undoes or annuls it, which is what a cancellation does.

clue.text: End of kids’ shows for kids

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: last letter
progs is short for programmes

explanation.surface: The closing moments of children's television programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprogs is British slang for children; progs is informal shorthand for programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is a colloquial British word for a child, so sprogs are young kids.

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the order of the two pieces flips

blocks.note: the M1, written MI, is Britain's main north-south motorway
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: A genuine race held on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' looks like an adjective, but in printing a literal is a typing error. In an across clue, 'on' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Among printers and editors a literal is a typographical mistake, a one-letter slip in type.

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its middle and keeps its ends

blocks.note: a prop is a support
single means one
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Backing the loudest, emptiest-headed fan in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' and 'supporter' seem to repeat each other; the first gives letters, the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent argues in favour of a cause or idea, so is an advocate or backer.

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to impede is to hold up
to air views is to express them

explanation.surface: A faulty express train caught in endless hold-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' conjures a train, but it is the verb to voice an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is damaged or weakened in function, so it is faulty or defective.

indicators.note: a rebound comes back the way it went, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: to radiate is to emit
E is the symbol for energy
mos, short for moments; in a flash means in a moment

explanation.surface: Light and energy flashing back, as on some past occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebounding' turns the whole run of three pieces round, not just the last. Sometime here means former, as in 'a sometime professor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime can mean former or at a past point, as does once in 'once a teacher'.

clue.text: Join commando, perhaps wiping out unit

indicators.note: to wipe something out is to remove it entirely, so a letter goes

blocks.note: a commando is one kind of soldier
one, a unit, is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Enlist as a commando and wipe out an enemy unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests a military group, but it is the number one, I, removed from SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: To solder is to fuse metal pieces together with melted alloy, so it means to join.

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming below, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval fleet setting off and meeting an ocean current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under way' reads as sailing, but in a down clue 'under' places the navy below the way. 'Current' is the adjective, not a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern and current both describe what belongs to the present day, up to date.

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words out loud to be written down, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: Rebels seized a fortress from a tyrant after a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here it is one who dictates aloud. In British speech FORT and FOUGHT are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Fought is the past tense of fight, meaning struggled or grappled, as in a wrestling bout.

indicators.note: to wreathe something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: grace is kindness or favour
the setter speaks of self as I, so 'this compiler is' becomes I'M

explanation.surface: The setter's face is wreathed in kindly smiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s looks possessive but stands for 'is': this compiler's = I'm. The surface smile turns out to be the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To face or pull a face is to make a twisted expression; a grimace is exactly that.

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: to face someone is to meet them
a pest is an irritation or nuisance

explanation.surface: Mounting annoyance, once confronted, blows up into a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising irritation' looks like one phrase, but 'rising' belongs to 'Faced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm, a literary word for a gale.

clue.text: Guide of sailor on oceans, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means according to what people say, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: oceans of something means lots, loads
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone navigating by a sailor's lore on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oceans' means a great quantity, LOADS, heard as LODES. In an across clue, 'on' puts the sailor after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is the Pole Star used in navigation, and figuratively any guiding principle.

clue.text: Sort of pen line with sweetheart

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
L is short for line
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter, a stock crossword device

explanation.surface: A romantic type of writer who pens lines to a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of pen' suggests a kind of writing tool, but 'Sort' is the definition and 'pen' is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is a type or kind, as in 'a new style of car', so it means sort.

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter
odium is hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A political manifesto that sets out to stir up hate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform' reads as a party programme, but the answer is a raised stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand for a speaker or winner, a kind of platform.

clue.text: Place of smallest room, some say

indicators.note: what some say is a matter of pronunciation, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the smallest room is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo

explanation.surface: Where the toilet is, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for toilet; LIEU is said the same way by many speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is French-derived for place, surviving in 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.

clue.text: Almost doesn’t start in good time

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: Someone almost never gets going on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lateness, which is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in good time is to arrive with time to spare, before the appointed hour.

clue.text: English bank backed charge creating stress

indicators.note: moving backwards means going the wrong way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: E is short for English
a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A British bank's reverse charges cause customers anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it is a row, as in a bank of seats; 'backed' turns only the first two pieces round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, often by repeating it over and over.

clue.text: Understand fitting, chaps? Time for alteration

blocks.note: to read a situation is to understand it
just means fitting or deserved
chaps are men
T is short for time

explanation.surface: A tailor tells customers who can see the fit is off that it needs altering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' suggests a tailor's fitting, but it means proper, JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A readjustment is a change made to something so it works again, so it is an alteration.
